class.name: NetwDatabase
class.brief_description: The schema registry and read/write surface of the persistence layer.
class.description:
Save one as a [code].tres[/code] file in the FileSystem, give it a [member backend], and name it from [method Netw.configure_persistence].
[codeblock] var db := preload("res://data/game.tres").duplicate()
db.open_slot(&"slot_2") db.declare_table(&"players", Netw.configure_schema(&"players"))
var record: NetwRecord = await db.table(&"players").fetch("valeria").wait() [/codeblock]
[b]Slots[/b] A slot is one independent save namespace. Choose one with [method open_slot] before the first schema registration locks the backend. Backends receive the selected slot when they initialize and scope every record under it. [codeblock lang=text] NetwDatabase └── open_slot(&"slot_2")
Backend namespace └── slot_2 ├── players │ └── valeria └── world └── chest_01 [/codeblock] [b]Schema drift[/b] When a loaded record carries columns the current schema does not declare, [member mismatch_policy] decides what happens to it.

method.name: current_slot
method.description: The active slot, [code]&"default"[/code] when [method open_slot] never ran.

method.name: declare_table
method.description:
Declares [param table] from [param schema], optionally binding [param record_script] as the [NetwRecord] subclass its reads hydrate into. [param schema] is a [NetwSchema], this is what gives the database the column types it needs to reject a value of the wrong shape instead of assigning it. A bare [Array] of column names is accepted as the untyped form, and a table declared that way coerces nothing. [codeblock] db.declare_table(&"rocks", Netw.configure_schema(&"rocks") .replicated(false), RockRecord)
db.declare_table(&"rocks", [&"health", &"position"]) # untyped [/codeblock] Declaring the same table again merges the new columns in.

method.name: delete_slot
method.description: Permanently removes [param slot] and every record under it, settling with an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. Works before [method open_slot].

method.name: erase
method.description: Permanently removes [param id] from [param table], settling with an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. A database with no [member backend] rejects with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED].

method.name: find
method.description: Reads the stored record for [param id] in [param table] and settles with it as a [Dictionary]. An absent record settles as an empty [Dictionary]. Rejects with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when the table has no declared schema or the database has no [member backend]. [codeblock] db.find(&"players", username).then( func(record: Dictionary) -> void: engine.apply(record), ) [/codeblock]

method.name: find_all
method.description: Reads every stored record in [param table] matching [param filter] and settles with them as an [Array] of [Dictionary]. An empty [param filter] returns the whole table. Similarly to [method find], rejects with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when the table has no declared schema or the database has no [member backend].

method.name: get_column_type
method.description: The declared [enum NetwMultiplayer.ColumnType] of one column, or [code]-1[/code] when the table was declared without types.

method.name: get_registered_columns
method.description: The column names registered for [param table], or an empty array when nothing has declared it yet.

method.name: list_slots
method.description: Lists all the slots backend holds, as an [Array] of [StringName]. [codeblock] for slot in await db.list_slots().wait(): print(slot) [/codeblock]

method.name: open_slot
method.description: Opens [param slot] as the active save namespace. The first call fixes the slot for this database instance.

method.name: table
method.description: A [NetwRecordTable] for [param table]. The handle is created per call and holds no cache, so asking twice costs one small object and returns the same table.

method.name: table_flush
method.description: Saves [param table]'s committed rows into [param into] as one record. The unit of commit and of hydrate is the whole table, because routes must be re-created as a set, so a table saves as one record rather than one record per row. Two thousand rows are one file on the file-system backend, not two thousand. [codeblock lang=text] db.<into> ┖╴<schema name> the one record ┠╴ids PackedStringArray, parallel to the row order ┖╴<column key> the committed storage array, verbatim [/codeblock] [param ids] names the row whose route is [code]session.table_read_routes(table)[i][/code]. Stable identity is the caller's domain, since they created the rows, and it is what lets a fresh session rebuild its own indexes from [method table_hydrate]. Save keys never ride the wire and routes never touch the disk. Values are the committed storage arrays, which quantization never touches, so a quantized column saves at full precision. A [constant NetwMultiplayer.COLUMN_ENTITY] column is skipped with one warning, because a route is meaningless in the session that loads it. The result is a [NetwPromise] because the write is a database write, and it settles with the [enum @GlobalScope.Error] the write reached. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK written ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED no table name, or session is not the server ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the handle names no table ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA ids.size() disagrees with the committed row count [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: table_hydrate
method.description: Loads [param table]'s saved record from [param into], creates fresh routes for its rows, and commits them into [param session]. See [NetwTableHandle] for more details on what table route are. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴routes PackedInt64Array freshly claimed, the committed row order ┖╴ids PackedStringArray parallel, the keys the flush wrote [/codeblock] Both arrays are empty when no record exists, which is the first-play case rather than an error. A [constant NetwMultiplayer.COLUMN_ENTITY] column zero-fills, matching the skip at [method table_flush]. The result is a [NetwPromise] settling with that [Dictionary], because the read is a database read and the rows are committed on the edge it settles. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: transaction
warm
method.description: Warms [param table] into the backend cache per [param request] at runtime, settling with an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. This is the escape hatch for driving warming from a game's own hooks, a scene load or a menu, rather than from [member warm_policy] at initialization. A synchronous backend has no cache to fill and returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK] without doing anything.

members.member: The storage this database reads and writes through. Assign it before the first read or write, which is what initializes the backend and locks the slot. A database with no backend rejects every call rather than dropping writes quietly.

What happens when a loaded record carries columns the current schema does not declare. The default is the least destructive reading: a stray column is dropped and the rest of the row loads, because a save file is the player's and a schema that grew a column is the ordinary case rather than corruption.

The per-table cache-warming strategy applied when the backend initializes, which is the first read or write. Assign [code]null[/code] to leave every table to lazy fetch-on-miss. Synchronous backends ignore it. Never assigned, this reads [code]null[/code] and warming runs through a stock [WarmPolicy], which warms everything. Assigning [code]null[/code] is therefore not the same as leaving it alone, and the two read alike from the getter: one turns warming off and the other is the untouched default.

signal.name: record_loaded
signal.description: Emitted after a record is read from the backend. [param hit] is [code]false[/code] when no record was found, which is a miss rather than a failure.

signal.name: schema_mismatch
signal.description: Emitted when a loaded record disagrees with the current schema. [param missing] is the columns the schema declares that the record does not carry. [param unknown] is the columns the record carries that the schema does not declare, which is what [member mismatch_policy] judges.

signal.name: schema_registered
signal.description: Emitted whenever a table's declared columns change. [param columns] is the full merged column list, not only the columns this declaration added.

signal.name: transaction_committed
signal.description: Emitted after a [method transaction] commits successfully, counting the tables and records the batch touched. A commit that returned an error announces nothing.

constants.constant: Delete the record and start fresh.
Strip the undeclared columns from the loaded data and proceed with the known ones. Columns the schema declares that the record does not carry take their scene defaults.
Reject the read with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] and leave the record unchanged.
